note: Mid-line wrap: a typed character mid-line triggers a wrap at an earlier space; the cursor stays on the first line and undo restores the pre-typing column.
Group break: a movement that returns to the wrap cursor (Home/End) followed by more typing; the second addition is a separate undo item from the wrap+trigger, which undo as one unit.

Two separate wraps, each its own undo group because hard_wrap closes the group with a last_kind reset; undo removes the second then the first, redo restores each. A single text step produces one hard_wrap call, so this is not two wraps in one addition group.
Autoindent wrap: the wrapped line receives the leading indent; undo restores the pre-typing cursor on the original indented line.

Spillage join with redo and continued editing: a second wrap joins the remainder onto the overflow; undo removes the join then the first wrap, redo restores each, and a further wrap after redo splits because the spillage pointer was cleared by undo (matching the reference). The continuation types ' fff' (three bytes): 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12, so the join would be accepted if the spillage pointer were still valid; the observed split therefore proves the pointer was cleared, not that the fill rejected the join.

Short-overflow / non-matching prefix: the overflow line 'd' is shorter than the 4-byte indent; the join must not strip a non-matching prefix nor panic. Saves the joined bytes (before undo) and checks the undo sequence.

Insert above the predecessor moves the live overflow one line down: Enter at column 0 of the predecessor 'aaaa bbbb ' leaves the predecessor on line 1 and the overflow 'cccc' on line 2, so the spillage marker has to follow the overflow's identity instead of its index. The next wrap types ' xy' (13 columns): the remainder 'xy' is 2 bytes and the moved overflow is 4 columns, so 2 + 4 = 6 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted; the saved bytes show the joined line 'xy cccc'. A stale index marker would leave the overflow unjoined and save 'xy' and 'cccc' on separate lines.

Delete that removes the target node: Delete at the end of the predecessor 'aaa bbb ccc ' joins it with the overflow 'ddd'. The reference frees the lower node of a line join, so the spillage pointer names a freed node and cannot be joined onto. The successor 'TAIL' stays below as an unrelated line. The next wrap types ' eee': the remainder 'ddd eee' is 7 bytes and 'TAIL' is 4 columns, so 7 + 4 = 11 <= fill 12 and the join would be accepted if the pointer were still valid; the saved bytes show the split 'ddd eee' above 'TAIL' instead of the join 'ddd eee TAIL'.

Redo after undo: after undo then redo of the spillage join, the spillage pointer must be cleared so a further wrap splits rather than joining (matching the reference's delete_node/clear-on-undo lifetime). The continuation types ' fff' (three bytes): 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12, so the join would be accepted if the pointer were valid.

Undo only the second wrap: the spillage pointer must be cleared by the undo so the next wrap splits (matching the reference). The continuation types ' fff' (three bytes): 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12, so the join would be accepted if the pointer were valid.

Saved-point round trip: save the first wrap (unmodified), edit (modified), undo the edit (unmodified, back at the saved point), undo the wrap (modified, past the saved point), redo the wrap (unmodified), redo the edit (modified). Explicitly asserts Modified absence/presence at each step.

Autoindent + spillage join with a matching indent prefix: the indented line '    aaa bbb ' wraps into the indented overflow '    ccc'. The second wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the overflow is 8 columns, so 3 + 8 = 11 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted. The reference strips the duplicated lead of the overflow when the two prefixes are equal, so the saved continuation is '    eee ccc'; without the strip it would be '    eee     ccc'.

Mismatching nonempty prefixes: the predecessor '  aaa bbb ' has a two-space lead and the live overflow '> ccc d' has a two-byte quote lead. The second wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the target is 7 columns, so 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted. The reference only strips the duplicated lead when the two prefixes are equal, so the saved continuation is 'eee > ccc d'; a strip that ignored the mismatch would save 'eee ccc d'.

Empty live target: the overflow 'ccc' is reduced to length zero by in-place deletions, which keep the node and its identity. The next wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the empty target is 0 columns, so 3 + 0 = 3 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted; the saved continuation is 'eee ' and the emptied line is consumed. If the target node had been freed the wrap would split and the file would keep the empty line.

Tabs: the fixture carries a literal 0x09 lead ('\taaa bbb'), not an interactively typed tab that would expand to spaces. With autoindent the wrap copies the tab lead to the continuation ('\tccc'). The second wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the target is 7 columns, so 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted. The reference strips the duplicated tab lead of the target when the prefixes match, so the saved continuation is '\teee ccc'; without the strip it would be '\teee \tccc'.
UTF-8 multibyte: a second wrap joining a remainder that ends in a multibyte character (€); the prefix-skip must respect character boundaries. Undo/redo and saved bytes.
The live target begins with a blank; an accepted join strips it and saves aa bb ccc  / eee fff ddd (see oracle recordings).
Fill-rejected join: the remainder plus overflow exceed the fill, so the join is rejected and the wrap splits instead. Undo/redo and saved bytes.
Trimblanks on (cursor before wrap point): the typed blank is protected; the trim removes only trailing break blanks after it. Valid cursor through undo/redo and saved bytes.

Decisive undo of Delete-join that removed the overflow: the final remainder ' fff' is three bytes and the next line 'eee ddd' is seven columns, so 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12 and marker validity (not fill rejection) determines the result. The reference does not restore the spillage pointer when undoing the Delete-join (undo JOIN creates a new node), so the subsequent wrap must split (fff above eee ddd), not join into 'fff eee ddd'.

Decisive Backspace-join equivalent of 020: position at the start of the spillage target and Backspace to join it into the predecessor. The final remainder ' fff' is three bytes and the next line 'eee ddd' is seven columns, so 3 + 7 = 10 <= fill 12 and marker validity determines the result. The reference does not restore the spillage pointer when undoing the Backspace-join (undo JOIN creates a new node), so the subsequent wrap must split (fff above eee ddd), not join into 'fff eee ddd'.
Divergent edit invalidates redo: after undo and one redo, a new edit (X) discards the remaining redo history; an explicit redo reports Nothing to redo and changes nothing.
Embedded NUL at byte offset 4 in fixture aaab\0bbb cccc remains before the actual split at byte 9; it must survive as a payload byte through wrapping and undo/redo.
Embedded NUL after the wrap point: fixture 'aaa bbb ccccc\0d'; the NUL is in the remainder and must survive the wrap split and undo/redo as a payload byte.

Decisive ordinary-addition redo continuation (integrated from the finder suite): wrap, separate non-wrapping addition, undo both, redo both, then wrap the predecessor again. The ordinary addition's history after-state carries the wrap's spillage generation; the reference's ADD redo never reassigns spillage_line, so the next wrap must split (eee on its own line) not join into 'eee ddd ee'.

Decisive whole-line cut of the spillage target: fixture 'aaa bbb ccc ddd\nTAIL\n'. Type X at End of line0 to create an overflow (spillage 'dddX'), then ^K cuts that overflow as a whole line, leaving ordinary successor text TAIL below the predecessor. A subsequent fill-accepted wrap (3 + 4 = 7 <= 12) of the predecessor must split (eee above TAIL), not join into 'eee TAIL', because the reference detaches the cut node into the cutbuffer and the spillage generation leaves the buffer.

Production NUL join through the live overflow target: fixture 'aaa bbb ccc dd\0dd\n' has a payload NUL in what becomes the spillage target. Typing X creates the spillage 'd\0ddX'; returning to the predecessor and typing ' eee' triggers an accepted second-wrap join whose assembled current line plus target contains the NUL. The production join path (hard_wrap -> decode_nuls -> Buffer::replace) must preserve the NUL as a payload byte (0x00) in the saved file, not reinterpret it as a line separator. A regression that removes decode_nuls from the production join corrupts the line structure and fails this case.

Explicit mark through a spillage join: the mark is set on the overflow 'ddd' at column 1, the predecessor then wraps again and joins the overflow. The reference moves the mark to the joined line and then to the continuation, so the mark ends at column 5 of 'eee ddd' and the cut removes only ' d' between the cursor and the mark; the saved bytes are 'aaa bbb ccc  ' and 'eeedd'. A mark that is clamped to the start of the replaced span cuts the whole buffer instead.

Delete that joins an empty predecessor with its successor: the predecessor is deleted down to length zero and Delete then joins it with the live overflow 'ddd'. The reference keeps the top node of a join and frees the lower node, so the spillage pointer names a freed node. The next wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the following line 'ddd' is 3 columns, so 3 + 3 = 6 <= fill 12 and the join would be accepted if the pointer were valid; the saved bytes show 'eee' above 'ddd'.

Backspace that joins an empty predecessor with its successor: the Backspace-equivalent of 029. The reference keeps the top node of a join and frees the lower node, so the spillage pointer names a freed node. The next wrap types ' eee': 3 + 3 = 6 <= fill 12 and the join would be accepted if the pointer were valid; the saved bytes show 'eee' above 'ddd'.

Partial multiline cut of the target: the marked cut runs from column 0 of the predecessor to column 1 of the overflow 'ddd'. The reference keeps the top node of a partial cut and detaches the bottom node, so the spillage pointer names a freed node and the remaining text is 'dd'. The next wrap types ' eee': 3 + 2 = 5 <= fill 12 and the join would be accepted if the pointer were valid; the saved bytes show 'eee' above 'dd'.

Quote prefix: the default quotestr matches the leading '> '. The reference copies the quote lead to the continuation line and restores the cursor to column 10 on redo, so the saved bytes are '> aaa bbb ' and '> ccc dddX'. Without the quote lead the continuation would be 'ccc dddX' and the cursor would be at column 8.

Continuation autoindent: the reference samples the next line when it is in the same paragraph and is not a paragraph start, so the continuation of '    aaa bbb ccc' gets the two-space indent of '  zzz' and not the four-space indent of the wrapped line; the saved bytes are '    aaa bbb ' and '  cccX'.

Nonpositive fill with line numbers: the reference wraps at the terminal width (80 columns) and not at the margin-reduced edit width, so a fill of 0 keeps the 78-byte line unwrapped and the saved file is one line ending in 'bbX'.

Negative fill with line numbers: the reference wraps at COLS + fill (80 - 8 = 72 columns) and not at the margin-reduced edit width, so the break is before 'ccc' and the saved second line is 'cccX' instead of 'bb cccX'.

One-character live target: the overflow 'ccc' is reduced to 'c' by in-place deletions, which keep the node and its identity. The next wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the target is 1 column, so 3 + 1 = 4 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted; the saved continuation is 'eee c'.

Paste into the live target: a bracketed paste of 'Z' at the start of the overflow 'ddd' turns it into 'Zddd' without freeing the node, so the spillage pointer still names it. The next wrap types ' eee': the remainder is 3 bytes and the target is 4 columns, so 3 + 4 = 7 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted; the saved continuation is 'eee Zddd'. A paste that cleared or retargeted the pointer would split instead.

Multi-line paste that shifts the live target: pasting 'X\nY' at the start of the predecessor inserts a line, so the overflow 'ddd' moves one line down. The spillage pointer names the target's identity, not its index, so it still names the overflow. The next wrap types ' eee' on the predecessor: the remainder is 3 bytes and the target is 3 columns, so 3 + 3 = 6 <= fill 12 and the join is accepted; the saved continuation is 'eee ddd'. A pointer that followed the index would have joined the wrong line.
A pre-existing mark on TAIL shifts down exactly once when a continuation is inserted above it; the marked cut removes only the selected newline, saving aaa bbb / cccdeTAIL.
Mark originally after the split follows the continuation once; marked cut keeps TAIL.
Mark after a split at EOF stays within the continuation; subsequent cut must not panic.
Join-origin mark after duplicated indentation receives prefix removal before the split.
Join-origin mark after extra blanks receives blank removal before the split.
A typing burst ending in a blank reaches the no-added-space join branch.
Forward selection after wrap cuts the typed suffix and preserves the following TAIL node.
Mark inside the stripped indentation maps to the join point rather than cutting surviving ccc.
Mark originally at byte 0 of the wrapping line; verify split boundary and direction, then cut.
Mark originally at byte 8 of the wrapping line; verify split boundary and direction, then cut.
Mark originally at byte 12 of the wrapping line; verify split boundary and direction, then cut.
Mark originally at byte 14 of the wrapping line; verify split boundary and direction, then cut.
Mark at byte 0 of live indented successor, before/inside/after stripped prefix; join then cut.
Mark at byte 1 of live indented successor, before/inside/after stripped prefix; join then cut.
Mark at byte 4 of live indented successor, before/inside/after stripped prefix; join then cut.
Mark at byte 6 of live indented successor, before/inside/after stripped prefix; join then cut.
Mark at byte 7 of live indented successor, before/inside/after stripped prefix; join then cut.
Mark moved by a pure split with utf8; subsequent cut, undo and redo.
Mark moved by a pure split with quote; subsequent cut, undo and redo.
Mark moved by a pure split with trim; subsequent cut, undo and redo.
